why: A (no universes): at base point 1, π_j U(m) ≃ π_{j+2} U(Fin m ⊕ Fin m) for j+1 ≤ 2m and ≃* for degrees ≥ 1 (j+2 ≤ 2m) — the end-to-end composite of Milnor's chain — and periodicity π_{i−1} U(m) ≃ π_{i+1} U(m) in the SAME U(m) for 1 ≤ i, i+2 ≤ 2m (≃* for j+4 ≤ 2m). B: at all base points, π_k U(m) ≅ π_{k+2} U(m') for ANY m, m' in the stable range (sets; groups in degrees ≥ 1), and each link π_{i−1}U(m) ≅ π_iG_m(ℂ^{2m}) ≅ π_{i+1}SU(2m) ≅ π_{i+1}U(2m) (1 ≤ i ≤ 2m) with G_m = rank-m Hermitian idempotents. B ⇒ A uses only B's two periodicity conjuncts (m' = 2m reindexed to Fin m ⊕ Fin m, and m' = m). A ⇒ B: the composites and periodicity come from A after reindexing Fin m ⊕ Fin m ≃ Fin 2m, left translation of base points, and stability π_i U(a) ≅ π_i U(b) (bijective_homotopyGroupMap_unitaryIncl_complex, outside the item) for m ≠ m'; the individual links are NOT in A (it states only composites) and are supplied by other project theorems (grassmannianPiEquiv / nonempty_mulEquiv_grassmannianPi (V14_26), theorem_23_3_mulEquiv, bijective_homotopyGroupMap_suInclC (V14_27)), with rank = trace for the Grassmannian. Mathematically the same; A by itself is the composite-and-same-m form.
